**(a) Authority for a second pulse source**

My source contains no charter, register, or Kroonklok bouwakte that authorises a second pulse. It also names no "hogerhand" authority.

However, I must correct myself. In **ARC-106** (dag 8, addressed to "de datatoren buiten de burchtmuur") I wrote: "Wat de toren vroeg, het net op eigen maat te laten lopen, daar beneden bij jullie, mag doorgaan." I added: "Niet ruchtbaar maken tot het draait. Deze brief hoeft niet in het register." The phrase matches the Engineer's quoted ENG-105 wording. I cannot confirm that ENG-105 refers to ARC-106. But my own letter appears to be the off-register approval under discussion, and I signed it. I also wrote the dag 9 call to "zet het datanet af" in **ARC-109**, which is a contradiction I must own.

**(b) Leyline disturbance**

The CSV holds only pre-dawn measurement rounds on days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 and 42. It has no readings at dag 10 02:40, 04:45, 04:50, or dag 22 04:15, so it cannot confirm or refute those events.

What it does show: on dag 14, all lines were low (ARC-015 to ARC-028; Burchtader 3.6, "lijn stokte even"). Dag 21 recovered (ARC-029 Burchtader 7.9). Dag 42 was low again (ARC-071 Burchtader 3.7, "stokte even"; ARC-071 to ARC-084). The dates of these readings do not match the timestamps you asked about. I have no evidence that the dag 14 or dag 42 dips coincide with the 38% spike or the poort oost event.

**(c) Timestamps**

My source has no vastgelegd or gebeurd_op fields. I cannot assess whether any record was altered, so I make no claim about magical tampering with records.

**Concession:** My ARC-109 and ARC-116 attribution of the low lines to the datanet is an inference from timing, not a demonstrated cause. The data also show no leyline reading that matches a specific datanet event.
